leads.title: ILGA-Europe Annual Report - Romania ranking 2022 / 2026
leads.documents: EU-wide LGBTQ rights protection ranking; documents Romania ranked 26 of 27 EU countries in 2022 behind all except Poland, and degraded to lowest-ranked EU country in 2026 report.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'advocacy group ILGA-Europe ranked Romania 26 out of 27' in 2022 and 'lowest ranked among all European Union countries' in 2026 report. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Emergency Ordinance no. 89/2001 repealing Penal Code Art. 200
leads.documents: Decriminalization of homosexuality; eliminates Art. 200 (1-5 years imprisonment for same-sex relations, 2-7 years with coercion/minor, etc.) and adjusts sex offences to avoid discrimination. Came into force January 2002 after President Ion Iliescu signed.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Adrian Nastase's government adopted the Emergency Ordinance no. 89/2001, which eliminated Art. 200' - in force January 2002. Prior history: 1937 Code Art.431, 1948 extension, 1957 removal of 'public scandal', 1968 Art.200, 1996 amendment to public only. No URL visible.

leads.title: Romania Constitutional Court Decision December 2020 on gender identity education ban
leads.documents: Strikes down June 2020 parliament amendment to education law placing blanket ban on gender identity studies passed without public debate; key transgender-expression / free expression protection.
leads.detail: Text states 'In June 2020, it placed a blanket ban on the study of gender identity in education. The ban was struck down in December 2020 by Romania's Constitutional Court.' Plus University of Bucharest condemnation quote. No URL visible.

leads.title: Constitution Art. 48 and Civil Code Art. 259 - marriage definition
leads.documents: Legal bar to same-sex marriage/family protection; Constitution defines family as 'freely consented marriage between spouses' but Civil Code Art.259(1) restricts to 'union between a man and a woman'; same-sex couple cannot receive state protection as family.
leads.detail: Quoted verbatim: 'Article 48 - Family (1) The family shall be founded on a freely consented marriage between spouses...' and 'Article 259 - Marriage (1) Marriage shall be a freely consented union between a man and a woman'. No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Justice - Coman and Others, June 2018
leads.documents: Residence rights for same-sex spouses; rules same-sex spouses have same right of residence if marriage legally performed in EU country, following Romanian Constitutional Court referral of Romanian-American couple married in Belgium.
leads.detail: Cited as 'European Court of Justice ruled in June 2018 in Coman and Others that same-sex spouses have the same right of residence'. No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 23 May 2023 Article 8 ruling
leads.documents: Finds Romania breaching Article 8 ECHR by not allowing same-sex couples to marry or register civil partnerships; documents lack of legal recognition despite 2018 high-court residency rulings.
leads.detail: Cited as 'On 23 May 2023 the European Court of Human Rights ruled that Romania is breaching article eight... by not allowing same-sex couples to marry or register civil partnerships.' Followed by PM Marcel Ciolacu Nov 2023 refusal. No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2021 ruling on 20 February 2013 Museum incident
leads.documents: Documents enforcement failure and anti-LGBTQ incident: ~50 protesters stopped screening of 'The Kids Are All Right' at Museum of the Romanian Peasant shouting 'Death to the homosexuals', filming attendees; Court found violation of Article 8 and 11 and discrimination on sexual orientation for failure to conduct effective investigation.
leads.detail: Incident dated 'evening of 20 February' during LGBTQ History Month; ruling dated 'In 2021, the European Court of Human Rights ruled that Romania violated Article 8 and Article 11'. No URL visible.

leads.title: National Council for Combating Discrimination (CNCD) - 2000 anti-discrimination law enforcement
leads.documents: Rights machinery; 2000 Parliament law outlawing sexual orientation discrimination in employment, goods/services, housing, education, health, audiovisual, justice; CNCD fines, e.g., TAROM fined for refusing same-sex partners couples discounts Valentine's Day 2005 and ordered to rectify.
leads.detail: Cited as law 'among the most comprehensive in the European Union, has been successfully tested by the National Council for Combating Discrimination (CNCD)' with TAROM example. Also 2006 Penal Code amendments on incitement and aggravating circumstance. No URL visible.

leads.title: CNCD September 2007 MSM blood donation ruling and Ministry of Health January 2008 law
leads.documents: Documents discriminatory MSM blood ban and equality-body remedy; CNCD ruled ban illegal creating 'hostile, degrading, humiliating and offensive atmosphere for homosexuals' and ordered removal; Ministry issued new law Jan 2008 removing ban, not yet implemented.
leads.detail: Cited as 'in September 2007, Romania's National Council for Combating Discrimination ruled that this ban was illegal' and 'In January 2008... Ministry of Health released a new law'. No URL visible.

leads.title: EU Fundamental Rights Agency 2013 LGBT survey / ACCEPT 2010 survey
leads.documents: Documented prevalence of anti-LGBTQ discrimination/violence in Romania; FRA ranks Romania third after Croatia and Bulgaria, 21% attacked/threatened in past 5 years; ACCEPT 2010: 68.2% suffered discrimination/exclusion, >50% insulted, 30% threatened, streets 49.5% main site.
leads.detail: Cited as '2013 survey by the European Union's Fundamental Rights Agency' and 'survey done by ACCEPT association in 2010'. Also CNCD 3 April 2012 'Perceptions and Attitudes Regarding Discrimination' report. No URL visible.
